libraries.name: curl_cffi
libraries.use_for: Primary HTTP client for WAF-protected Indian financial sites (Akamai on NSE/BSE, Cloudflare on CDSL/Acuite, Tata CDN on CRISIL, CloudFront/Entra on ICRA)
pros: Impersonates real Chrome/Firefox/Safari TLS (JA3/JA4) and HTTP/2 SETTINGS fingerprints via curl-impersonate / BoringSSL
Requests-compatible synchronous Session API plus native asyncio AsyncSession
Actively maintained (PyPI v0.17.0, 6.9k+ GitHub stars, pushed 2026-11-23); battle-tested by aeron7/nsepython against NSE Akamai Bot Manager
Orders of magnitude faster and lighter than headless browsers (~MBs RAM vs hundreds of MBs for Chromium)
cons: Cannot execute JavaScript challenges (Cloudflare Turnstile, Angular/React SPAs like India Ratings or DBIE)
C-extension binary wheels (manylinux/macOS/Windows) slightly heavier to build in minimal Alpine containers than pure Python

libraries.name: httpx
libraries.use_for: Clean async/HTTP2 client for open JSON APIs, RSS feeds, and non-TLS-fingerprinted endpoints (NSDL API/CSV, SEBI RSS/HTML, RBI RSS, CRISIL JSON servlet, local FastAPI/Flask internal services)
pros: Clean sync + async API, native HTTP/2 support (via h2), strict timeouts, connection pooling, custom transports/hooks
Pure Python (easy packaging, PyPI v0.28.1, 15.8k+ GitHub stars)
Used by BennyThadikaran/NseIndiaApi with FileCookieStore + pyrate_limiter
cons: Uses Python stdlib OpenSSL TLS fingerprint — immediately flagged (HTTP 403) by Akamai Bot Manager on NSE homepage and strict Cloudflare rules

libraries.name: requests
libraries.use_for: Simple synchronous scripts and legacy wrappers (jugaad-data, BseIndiaApi, nsetools) on unprotected or header-only endpoints
pros: Ubiquitous API (54.7k+ GitHub stars), huge ecosystem, zero learning curve
Session cookie jar + urllib3 Retry adapter well understood
cons: HTTP/1.1 only (no HTTP/2) and exposes standard OpenSSL TLS fingerprint (blocked by NSE AkamaiGHost)
Synchronous-only (blocks asyncio event loops without thread pools)

pros: Real Chromium/Firefox/WebKit engine executes full JavaScript, handles dynamic SPAs, and allows intercepting XHR JSON payloads
First-party Python sync and async APIs (PyPI v1.65.2, 15.1k+ GitHub stars); used by niks-data/sebi-rbi-regulatory-scraper
cons: High CPU/RAM footprint (~150-400 MB per browser context) and slow startup/render latency
Default Playwright leaks automation signals (navigator.webdriver) to Akamai/Cloudflare Bot Manager unless mitigated; overkill for JSON/RSS/SSR sources

operational_hardening.rate_limiting: Token-bucket per-domain rate limiters (e.g. pyrate_limiter as in NseIndiaApi or mthrottle as in BseIndiaApi): <=1-2 req/s for rating agencies & CDSL, <=3 req/s for exchanges, >=5s delay between bulk pagination pages (matching india-isin-data).
operational_hardening.retry_and_backoff: Differentiate permanent 404/400 from transient 429/5xx/WAF HTML-200 blocks. Use exponential backoff with full jitter (e.g. base 1s * 2^attempt + jitter, cap 30-60s) and honor Retry-After headers; never retry HTTP 404 or 401/418 endlessly.
operational_hardening.caching: Two-tier cache: (1) local SQLite/disk cache with source-appropriate TTLs (ISIN static facts: 7-30 days; rating rationales: 24h-7d; RSS circulars: 1-6h) + negative caching (short TTL on not-found) and conditional GETs (ETag / Last-Modified) for bulk CSVs/RSS.
operational_hardening.schema_drift_defenses: Validate every response before parsing (check Content-Type != text/html when expecting JSON, verify required keys like .count / .data / .docs as india-isin-data and src/bond_master/nsdl.py do), emit structured failure codes (FAILURE_BLOCKED, FAILURE_MALFORMED, FAILURE_PARSE_ERROR) and health metrics, and preserve snapshot fallback so upstream HTML/WAF drift degrades gracefully.
operational_hardening.robots_and_tos_discipline: Check and cache robots.txt per domain (respecting CRISIL's explicit crawler rules, SEBI's /js /css disallows, ICRA's sitemap guidance, and CDSL's Content-Signal headers); never scrape authenticated/PII portals (SCORES, SmartODR, CARE OTP flows); prefer official RSS/bulk CSV/API feeds and commercial data licenses (e.g. S&P Global/CRISIL, Acuite redistribution agreements) if moving beyond personal/tracker usage.
